_comment: One trimmed row per institution, plus the national rankings and the state rollup, for the assistant to look figures up in.

Field names are abbreviated; 'fields' below is the mapping and is authoritative. A field that is absent from a row means no data, never zero: an institution with no federal block was not surveyed, it did not spend nothing.

Non-resident is a visa category, not a birthplace, so every share here is a floor on the foreign-born proportion. fpd is an intensity ratio and not a price -- read fps and fpp beside it before quoting it, because the top of that ranking is medical schools where the denominator covers a fraction of the output.
Shares in 'states' are recomputed from the sums, never averaged across institutions.

fields.ms: non-resident share of those master's, pct
fields.mc: change in that share since 2010-2014, percentage points
fields.ds: non-resident share of those doctorates, pct
fields.dc: change in that share since 2010-2014, percentage points
fields.gs: non-resident share of graduate enrolment, pct
fields.fo: federal obligations from all agencies FY2023, USD
fields.ft: S&E fellowships, traineeships and training grants FY2023, USD
fields.fpd: federal obligations per core-STEM research doctorate per year, USD
fields.fps: core-STEM as a share of all research doctorates, pct -- how much of the doctoral output the fpd denominator covers
fields.fpp: professional doctorates awarded 2015-2022 (MD, DDS, JD) -- large here means fpd is measured against a small part of the output

sources.federal_obligations: NSF Federal Support Survey FY2023 (NSF 25-339 Table 17)

national_per_doctorate.note: Every institution nationally that clears the floor, so this is a wider population than the figure quoted on the funding page, which covers this project's own university set.
